title: region-readiness-validator-terraform-health-gates
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build an automated region readiness validator and Terraform-based health gates that can be executed from CI/CD and the Redwood Console to validate private (VPC) deployments prior to and during cross-region recovery or upgrades.

Scope:
- Terraform modules and remote-state patterns to create ephemeral verification stacks in a target region without changing production routing.
- A set of health-gate checks (gRPC readiness, token-scoped latency histogram, KV-cache consistency probe, storage replication lag, and control-plane API consistency).
- An orchestration shim (stateless Lambda / cloud-run job) that runs the sequence: create-ephemeral infra -> bootstrap lightweight canary workloads -> run health gates -> publish result (pass/fail + artifacts) -> tear down infra.
- Integration points: private deployment terraform modules, Console rollout UI (readiness API), Alerting (PagerDuty/Slack), and Upgrade playbooks.

Non-goals: full traffic cutover automation, stateful dataset migration tooling, or vendor-specific DR orchestration beyond standard Terraform and CI runners. This ticket focuses on verification automation and safe promotion signals to operators.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
1) Module granularity: We decided on two module layers: a thin "validator-infra" module (VPC peering / temporary route add / ephemeral compute) and "validator-boot" module (canary services + probes). This keeps production modules untouched and minimizes blast radius.
2) Remote state: Use customer-backed remote-state when present (S3/Google storage) and fallback to a Redwood-managed ephemeral bucket for exercise runs. Trade-off: additional permissions vs easier isolation.
3) Probe architecture: Use a mix of active (synthetic requests) and passive (metrics compare) checks. Active checks are more deterministic; passive checks are less invasive for production.
4) Runtime upgrades vs infra-only verification: For major runtime changes we include a staged compatibility test (small canary with pinned model artifact). For minor point upgrades, infra-only verification is allowed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform modules published to internal registry with examples and documented inputs/outputs.
- A CI job template that runs the validator against a non-prod and a private region sandbox.
- A console endpoint that can display latest run result, artifacts (logs, latency histograms), and fail reason.
- Automated roll back guidance in Console if a run fails during an upgrade window.

Deliverables & artifacts:
- RFC/Confluence: "Region Readiness Validator - Architecture" (link in links).
- GitHub: repo modules/validator-infra and modules/validator-boot (PR links in links).
- Terraform examples for AWS/GCP private deployments.
- CI templates for GitHub Actions and CircleCI.
- Console integration doc for rollout teams.

Operational notes:
- Default SLO thresholds: 95th percentile token latency < 350ms (read/write separate), KV cache sync errors < 0.5%, storage replication lag < 10s. These are configurable per-customer.
- Results should produce structured artifacts: prometheus snapshots, test transcripts, and a short diagnosis string for the Console.

Risks:
- Ephemeral infra provisioning failure could generate noise; mitigated by a timeout and retry policy with exponential backoff.
- Permissions escalation if customers grant Terraform more rights than intended; mitigated with least-privilege example modules and an opt-in Redwood-managed mode.

Next steps:
- Finalize module input schema and remote state strategy (this week).
- Complete initial GH PR for validator-infra.
- Security review request for module artifacts and ephemeral bucket usage.
